content.title: About
content.content: Chestnut flour is made from dried and finely ground sweet chestnuts (Castanea sativa). It has a light brown color, a mildly sweet nutty aroma, and a soft texture. It is used in baking, gluten‑free cooking, and as a thickening agent.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chestnuts belong to the beech family and differ from true nuts because their seeds are not encased in a hard shell.
Chestnut flour has a long tradition in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines.
Unlike wheat flour, chestnut flour is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Chestnuts are rich in complex carbohydrates and have a low glycemic index.
The flour retains some of the antioxidants found in whole chestnuts.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Chestnut flour provides thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: High fiber content aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with other nut flours, chestnut flour contains less fat, making it lighter.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: It supplies potassium, magnesium and iron, important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds in chestnuts help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Nut and chestnut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chestnuts.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Chestnut flour contains natural sugars; people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Storage sensitivity
items.content: Improper storage can cause the flour to oxidize and lose its flavor.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Chestnut flour can be used in gluten‑free baking (bread, cakes, pancakes), as a thickener in sauces, for breading, and in desserts to add a nutty flavor. It can often replace wheat flour 1:1, though additional liquid may be needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
